title: The goddess who is Vishnu's sleep
hookLine: the first story: Vishnu asleep on the waters, two demons rising, and Brahma praising the goddess who is Vishnu's sleep
carry: the goddess's power moves even the gods

lines: ONLY WATER, AT THE END OF AN AGE.
cards: No land. Only water, everywhere, at the end of an age. On it Vishnu lies asleep on the great serpent.

From his navel grows a lotus, and on it sits Brahma, the creator. Then, out of the dirt in Vishnu's ears, two demons are born: Madhu and Kaitabha. They see Brahma on his flower and decide to kill him.
Brahma looks down at Vishnu, the one who could protect him. Vishnu doesn't move. This is the sage Medhas's first story, and the goddess is in it from the start, though not where you'd look.

teach.b: Brahma doesn't shake Vishnu or call his name. He turns to the sleep itself. Here Vishnu's sleep has a name, Yoganidra, and she is the goddess.
So Brahma praises her. In paraphrase: you hold up this world, create it, protect it, and at the end take it back.
You are the great knowledge and the great illusion, the dark night at the end of things, and beauty, modesty and understanding. Who could praise you enough, when you put even Vishnu to sleep?
Then a request: wake him, and confuse these two demons.
The goddess answers, drawing out of Vishnu's eyes, mouth, nostrils, arms, heart and chest. Vishnu wakes and fights them for a very long time. Then the strangest moment.
Confused by the great illusion and proud of their strength, the demons tell Vishnu they're pleased with him: ask us a boon. He asks: be killable by me.
Caught, they look at the water everywhere and add a condition: then kill us where the earth isn't covered with water.
Vishnu lifts them onto his thigh, dry ground above the flood, and kills them there. So the goddess isn't a helper standing beside Vishnu. She's the power inside his sleeping and his waking.
That's the teaching of this book, named plainly: Shakti, the goddess, is the power that moves even the gods; without her, many devotees say, even the greatest god lies still.
And yesterday's confusion is at work in the demons: outwitted by their own pride.

how: Brahma's praise of Yoganidra in the first chapter of the Devi Mahatmya is recited as part of the whole text, and some Hindus who recite the Chandi treat the first chapter as its own opening section.

o: the glory of the goddess, told as a sage's stories
the story of how Vishnu made the world from water
a book of rules for kings who have lost a war

games.q: the first story — tap the pairs.
p: two demons born from Vishnu's ears
sits on the lotus from Vishnu's navel

s: Brahma wakes Vishnu by shaking him
he praises the goddess Yoganidra, Vishnu's sleep, and asks her to wake him.
the demons offer Vishnu a boon
confused and proud of their strength, they tell him he may ask them for one.
the demons ask to be killed in the water
they ask to be killed where the earth is not covered with water, and he lifts them onto his thigh.

games.q: you're Madhu and Kaitabha. you've just promised Vishnu he can kill you. water covers everything. what condition do you add?
o: kill us only after a thousand years.
kill us where the earth is not covered with water.
kill us only in battle with weapons.
games.why: they think there's nowhere dry. Vishnu lifts them onto his thigh, dry ground above the flood, and kills them there.

practice: Close the eyes and follow the order the text gives as the goddess leaves Vishnu: let attention wake in the eyes behind the lids, then the mouth, the nose and its breath, the arms, the heart, the chest, one place at a time, without forcing.
If you pray, greet the goddess by a name your family uses, Durga, Amba, Ma; if not, let the breath be the greeting.

wordCard.voice: The Devi Mahatmya. Today, its first story: the goddess as Yoganidra, the sleep of Vishnu, who leaves him so he can wake.

orig.note: Sanskrit: yoga-nidrā, yogic sleep. In the Devi Mahatmya, the goddess as the sleep of Vishnu.

carryVoice: Your line: the goddess's power moves even the gods. In this book, even Vishnu's sleep is Shakti. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Devi Mahatmya, chapter 1 (Madhu and Kaitabha; Brahma's hymn to Yoganidra)
